title: Build a directory tree that sizes itself

task.text: A file and a folder should answer the same questions, so callers never ask which one they hold.
`Node` and `File` are given. Implement the **composite**: `Dir` in `Dir.java`.

items: `Dir(String name, Node... children)` and `Dir(String name, List<Node> children)`; a `Dir` keeps its own copy of the list.
`size()` is the sum of its children's sizes; `fileCount()` the sum of theirs (an empty `Dir` has 0).
`find(name)` checks the `Dir` itself first, then each child in order, depth-first.
Work through the `Node` interface only: `Dir` must not test what kind of child it holds.

checks.title: An empty Dir is size 0 with no files
fileCount counts leaves at any depth
find locates files and Dirs by name
Dir copies the list it is given
Dir is a Node holding a List of children
Dir never asks what kind a child is
Dir works with a Node it has never seen

hints.text: A `Dir` is a `Node` that contains `Node`s. Because a child can be a `File` or another `Dir`, ask the child; each kind of `Node` knows how to answer for itself.

Store `List.copyOf(children)` in a `private final List<Node>`. `size()` and `fileCount()` map over the children through the `Node` interface and sum. The varargs constructor can delegate to the list one.
